newsitem.title: ITALY: Armed group takes over famous Venice belltower.
newsitem.headline: Armed group takes over famous Venice belltower.

text.p: A group believed to be armed crashed through the entrance of the belltower in Venice's St Mark's Square in a car on Friday and occupied it to demand a separate state in northern Italy, police said.

Italian state radio said more than a hundred police had surrounded the monument by the Grand Canal and that the group, believed to number five or six, had unfurled a flag of the former Venetian Republic.

The report said that shortly after midnight the men had forced the captain of a small ferry they had boarded to dock by the square. They then drove their vehicle to the base of the belltower and used it to smash through the door of the monument.

Police said they suspected the men, reportedly dressed in military fatigues, were part of a group which has been interrupting television broadcasts in the north with political slogans demanding a separate state.
Their action appeared timed to coincide with the 200th anniversary of the end of the Venetian Republic on May 12.

Italian radio said the men were demanding to speak "to our ambassador". It was not clear who this was, but reports speculated they wanted to speak to a member of the Northern League, which wants a separate state in the wealthy north of Italy.
